findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the oracle-source contradiction: the parent epic names 'a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK' as the harness, but the leaf uses `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and explicitly rejects the SDK — update the parent's Approach step 5 to name the pycontribs image as the chosen approach (and move the SDK rejection rationale there), then re-review, before this leaf can be treated as a valid subset.

Leaf Approach: 'Use the purpose-built test image that pycontribs/jira publishes for exactly this problem: pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1'

Leaf explicitly rejects: 'Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's atlas-run-standalone. It also yields a licensed local Jira, but it needs the full SDK toolchain and its licenses are short-lived (3-day timebombs requiring atlas-mvn clean recycling)'
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the oracle image source in direct contradiction with the parent. The parent's Approach step 5 names 'a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK at localhost:2990' as the oracle, and notes 'the same approach pycontribs/jira itself uses in its tests/conftest.py' as a parallel (not a source). The leaf instead uses 'pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' (a pycontribs-published Docker image) and explicitly rejects the Atlassian SDK approach as an alternative. Under G7's conflict rule the parent is authoritative; the leaf cannot diverge without first updating the parent.
findings.location: Leaf Approach section ('Use the purpose-built test image that pycontribs/jira publishes…') and 'Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's atlas-run-standalone'; Parent Approach step 5 ('the oracle is a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK at localhost:2990')
scenarios: An implementer following the parent epic expects the Atlassian SDK toolchain; the leaf delivers a different image source with different auth and startup mechanics.

If the parent's AC ('operator-attested full reconcile pass runs green against the Dockerized Jira') was written assuming the SDK image, the leaf's different image could produce a harness that satisfies the leaf but fails the parent's operator-attestation check.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the parent epic's Approach step 5 to read: 'Verify against a real Jira. Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle is the pycontribs/jira-test-image Docker image (pinned to 8.17.1) at localhost:2990 — the purpose-built image pycontribs/jira itself validates against. The Atlassian SDK atlas-run-standalone was considered and rejected because its licenses are 3-day timebombs hostile to repeatable CI.' Then re-submit the parent for re-review, after which J5 becomes a clean subset.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a maximum poll duration (e.g. 5-minute deadline with exponential backoff) and a terminal 'harness not running / Jira did not become ready within Xs' error in the readiness probe so the failure-path AC is mechanically satisfiable.

findings.finding: The readiness probe is specified as 'polls until the instance answers REST' with no stated maximum poll duration, retry count, or timeout. Jira 8.17.1 takes 2–4 minutes to boot; if the container starts but Jira never becomes healthy (OOM, bad image layer, port conflict, disk pressure), the probe loops indefinitely, hanging the test runner and any CI job that invoked it — with no 'harness not running' error, just a silent hang. The failure-path AC ('fails with a clear harness not running message from the readiness probe') cannot be satisfied by an unbounded loop.
findings.location: Approach section — readiness probe; Testing section — failure path AC
scenarios: Container starts but Jira OOMs during boot → probe loops forever → CI job times out with no meaningful message
Port 2990 is already in use → Jira never binds → infinite poll loop
Slow CI runner where Jira takes >N minutes → accidental hang
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'The readiness probe retries with exponential backoff for a maximum of 5 minutes; on deadline it raises RuntimeError("Jira DC harness did not become ready within 300 s — is the container running? (docker ps)") rather than a raw connection error.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In `docker-compose.yml` (and the `docker run` example in the README), restrict the port binding to loopback-only (`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`) or add an explicit, justified rationale in `tests/live_jira_dc/README.md` for why all-interface binding is acceptable in the target CI environment.
evidence: Plan states `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`
CI credentials are `admin/admin` (admin) and `jira_user/jira` (user) — publicly documented defaults
No statement that the compose port binding is loopback-restricted, nor any network-isolation rationale

T10(b2): endpoint access contract requires either a named auth mechanism OR an explicit justified no-auth/loopback rationale; all-interface binding with trivially-guessable credentials is the worst-case combination and must be explicitly addressed
findings.finding: The plan specifies `docker run -p 2990:2990` (and implicitly a docker-compose port mapping), which binds the Jira web UI and REST API to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0:2990), not loopback only. The plan provides no rationale for why all-interface binding is acceptable rather than loopback-restricted (`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`). On a shared CI build server or a developer machine on a corporate/office network, this exposes a Jira admin UI protected only by the well-known credential `admin/admin` to every host on the local network — yet the plan neither documents this risk, names a compensating control, nor justifies the broader binding.
findings.location: Approach section — `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990`; docker-compose.yml (new file, port mapping unspecified)
scenarios: Shared CI build server: any process or user on the same host or same network segment can reach the Jira admin UI at port 2990 and log in as admin with admin/admin during the test run
Developer machine on a corporate network: the Jira instance is reachable by colleagues for the duration of the test, potentially allowing data injection that corrupts teardown assertions
findings.suggested_fix: In docker-compose.yml set `ports: - '127.0.0.1:2990:2990'` and update the `docker run` example to `-p 127.0.0.1:2990:2990`. Add one sentence to the README: 'The port is bound to loopback only; the instance is not reachable from the network during test runs.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare the intended access posture for the Jira test container's port binding in the compose file and `jira-dc-up` target; if loopback-only (as the plan's own description implies), use `127.0.0.1:2990:2990` instead of `2990:2990` to prevent 0.0.0.0 exposure on shared/networked hosts.
evidence: Plan text: `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`
Plan text: `reachable at http://localhost:2990/jira`
Docker default: `-p 2990:2990` without a host-IP prefix binds to `0.0.0.0:2990`, not `127.0.0.1:2990`
Well-known credentials `CI_JIRA_ADMIN=admin / CI_JIRA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin` transmitted over plain HTTP on the exposed interface
Access posture is never declared (public / internal-only / loopback-only)
findings.finding: The `docker run` command and compose file use `-p 2990:2990` without an explicit `127.0.0.1:` host-bind prefix. Docker's default behavior binds to `0.0.0.0:2990`, making the unauthenticated Jira instance (with publicly known `admin/admin` credentials) reachable from any host on the network of the CI machine or developer workstation — not just loopback. The plan describes the service as 'reachable at http://localhost:2990/jira' but does not declare the intended access posture (loopback-only vs. network-wide), which is itself the gap.
findings.location: Approach section (`docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 ...`), Scope section (`tests/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`), Makefile `jira-dc-up` target
scenarios: On a shared CI runner, another job or tenant on the same host network can reach the Jira admin UI/API with `admin/admin` during the test run.
On a developer machine connected to an office or home LAN, any host on that network can reach the instance while it is running.
In a container-based CI environment with a shared network namespace (e.g. GitHub Actions with `network: host`), the surface is wider than loopback.
findings.suggested_fix: In `tests/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`, change the port mapping to `ports: ['127.0.0.1:2990:2990']`. Update the example `docker run` command in the Approach section to `docker run -dit -p 127.0.0.1:2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`. Add a one-line access-posture declaration to the README: 'This instance is loopback-only (`127.0.0.1:2990`); it must not be exposed on a network interface.'

Plan quote: 'the teardown oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls each issue's direct REST endpoint (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`) until it returns 404' — identical to the existing harness's contract.

The existing code is private to a test module (not an installable library), so true import reuse requires either extracting to `tests/_jira_teardown.py` or a deliberate 'copy-for-DC-context' decision — neither is stated.
findings.finding: The teardown oracle mechanics — poll each issue's direct REST endpoint until 404, assert 2xx on each delete call, never consult search — are already codified in `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` as `ArtifactTracker`, `_bilateral_teardown`, and the ADR 0037 §3 discipline. The plan re-specifies them from scratch for `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` without acknowledging the existing implementation or stating a deliberate decision to re-implement vs. extract to a shared helper.
findings.location: Approach section (teardown oracle paragraph) and Testing section (teardown oracle bullet)
scenarios: An implementer writes a fresh poll-until-404 loop that diverges from the battle-tested backoff in `_retry` (e.g. no sleep cap, no exhaustion log), producing a weaker teardown guarantee than the one already proven by `test_teardown_exhaustion_records_leak_and_reports`.
The ADR 0037 §3 discipline is extended (e.g. leaked-artifact logging) in one place but not the other, causing the two harnesses to drift silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `_retry`, the poll-until-404 loop, and the leaked-artifact log append into `tests/_jira_harness.py` (a shared test helper, not under any tier), then import from both `test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` and the new `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a structural confinement mechanism for `tests/live_jira_dc/` (e.g. a conftest.py fixture that auto-applies the `integration` marker to every item under the directory, mirroring what `tests/external/conftest.py` does for `external`) so exclusion cannot be broken by a missing per-file `pytestmark`.
evidence: 'Every test in the directory carries the existing `integration` marker — not a new custom marker — because `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (`Makefile:154`), so the suite is excluded by construction with no Makefile change'

findings.finding: The plan places tests in a new top-level directory `tests/live_jira_dc/` and relies on each test file carrying `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration` to stay out of the default suite. However, unlike `tests/external/`, there is no structural enforcement mechanism: `tests/conftest.py`'s `pytest_collection_modifyitems` only auto-applies and confines the `external` marker by directory; the `integration` marker has no analogous auto-apply or misplacement guard. A test added to `tests/live_jira_dc/` without the marker silently joins the default `make test` run. The plan's own gating oracle ('`pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` reports 0 tests') is a one-time check, not a persistent structural guard, so it cannot prevent future regression.
findings.location: Approach section — marker strategy; Testing section — gating oracle AC
scenarios: Developer adds test_harness_teardown.py to tests/live_jira_dc/ without the pytestmark line → live Docker test joins the default suite and fails on any machine without the container running
Future refactor forgets to copy pytestmark into a new test module in the directory
findings.suggested_fix: In `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`, add a `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook (or a `pytestmark` at conftest scope if pytest supports it) that auto-adds `pytest.mark.integration` to every collected item whose path is under `tests/live_jira_dc/`, eliminating dependence on per-file marker discipline.

findings.finding: The plan's teardown oracle asserts correctness by 'querying the project and finding it empty', but Jira's search index lags both creates and deletes by an unbounded interval. ADR 0037 §3 (already codified in the repo) explicitly prohibits post-deletion index assertions for exactly this reason, noting that a re-search of an already-deleted issue can return stale results and produce a false-clean or false-dirty teardown verdict. The plan's teardown oracle could pass (project appears empty) while issues are still indexed, or fail (project appears non-empty) while deleted issues are still visible — contradicting the project's own hard-won design principle.
findings.location: Testing section — 'teardown oracle' paragraph; also AC3 ('scratch project contains zero leftover issues')
findings.suggested_fix: Assert teardown success by issuing a direct GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key} for each created issue and expecting 404, rather than running a JQL search. This is index-free and matches ADR 0037's 'authoritative signal' principle.

findings.finding: The plan introduces a new opt-in gating mechanism ('a pytest marker plus an env flag') for tests/live_jira_dc/ without naming either, alongside a new top-level test directory — when the codebase already has a multi-layered, registered gating surface (REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL env var; tests/external/ auto-marking in tests/conftest.py; 'external', 'live', 'jira_live', 'integration' markers in pyproject.toml with --strict-markers). A third parallel tier/marker/env-var triple is config-surface proliferation; the plan should explain why the existing 'live' marker (already registered: 'live: live Jira reconciler-validation tests … excluded from the default run') or the 'external' tier cannot serve this need.

If a distinct directory is needed, explicitly name the new marker in the plan and show it is registered in pyproject.toml, and explain why `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` cannot serve as the env flag.
